metadata.title: Switching the a0 Law Off Where the Cold Component Sits: Theorems, a KiDS Test, and a Closed Class (Working Note)
metadata.description:
Working note, version 1.1 (2026-11-09; v1.0: DOI 10.5281/zenodo.24094860). AI-assisted research programme; not peer reviewed; not reproduced by any outside group. kappa = 1/2 is fitted; the theory is not closed; nothing here says the data favour this framework over any other.

This note does not complete the theory. It closes one class of completion. The record needs a cold clustering component at the CMB, none of it in galaxies beyond the phantom of the galaxy law g_N = g^2/(g + a0), and its presence in clusters. One reading would give all three: the law acts only inside regions around galaxies that have been cleared of the component, and the component, with ordinary gravity, is everywhere else. We ask whether any action can deliver that reading.

For every switch that multiplies the law's Lagrangian we show, with the algebra certified in Lean 4 (72 theorems, standard axioms only, each file with a twin of false statements that fails): a spherical law-on region shows only its baryons from outside; such regions boost large-scale gravity in proportion to the volume they fill; and the force on whatever carries the switch has an exact closed form bounded by a0 M_b. Six lanes then grade the class, each with criteria frozen before any number, known answers and a mutation twin. Two independent lanes confirm that CMB lensing lets law-on regions fill about 2 % of space (0.0231; 0.0197 at 2 sigma with growth), against the 0.29 needed to keep the law on over the range of the KiDS weak-lensing radial acceleration relation. A test on 181,477 KiDS lenses, whose primary statistic a second session re-derived blind, passes the law at its frozen gate (host-free outer amplitude 1.098 +- 0.154 / 0.999 +- 0.141 of the law; the regrade reads NOT SEPARATED on one footing through a tie rule) and shows, in a calibration-free form, that what lies outside a wall must weigh at least 23 baryon masses per galaxy, four times the share the record assigns. The wall's force cannot clear or carry that much, statically or dynamically. Every exit of the class therefore has a failing verdict.

Also reported: what the KiDS test does not decide (the law as a lens's own field against a heavy exterior), the dependence of the outer points on the gas mass at Mpc radii, an edge effect of projected isolation cuts, three wrong pre-freeze estimates of our own, and two corrections to earlier lanes. The supplement zip holds every lane file (criteria, amendments, scripts, outputs, mutation outputs, results) and the Lean files with their twins.

Version 1.1 adds one disclosure to the Method section and one qualifier, and changes no number or label: two mutation arms (SWT1's wall-pressure arm and GAL1's sign arm) did not bite as frozen; both are disclosed in their lanes and neither label uses them. The allowance for regions that exist from z = 6 is marked as computed after the freeze.
